rules.quote: Don’t use blogs for essential information that should be stand-alone content.
rules.violation_condition: essential information that should be stand-alone content published as a blog post
rules.why: G-5 vs text rule: explicitly forbids publishing essential stand-alone information in blogs.

rules.quote: Don’t duplicate information that’s available elsewhere.
rules.violation_condition: blog content that duplicates information available elsewhere
rules.why: Clear negative instruction regarding blog content.

covers.quote: Start with a title that helps users understand what the post is about. Include keywords.

parts.quote: How to get mental health support
Tips for making a grant application
Need support? Here’s what you need to know
Get your application in now – time is running out

rules.specification: Blog titles should clearly inform users what the post is about and avoid sensationalized or vague clickbait phrasing.
rules.violation_condition: a blog title written as clickbait rather than clearly stating what the post is about
rules.why: G-2, G-4: covers the title guidance and directly backed by Write this / Not this examples.

covers.quote: Cover one main idea per paragraph.

rules.quote: Keep paragraphs to a maximum of 2 to 3 sentences so people can read them on mobile devices.
rules.violation_condition: a paragraph in a blog post containing more than 3 sentences
rules.why: Specific, checkable formatting rule for blog paragraphs.

examples.note: Example of a call to action

parts.quote: To bookmark the topics you find most useful, visit the Style Manual.

rules.quote: Include a call to action at the end of your post.
rules.specification: The final section or block of a blog post should contain a call to action, such as an invitation or link to next steps, feedback, subscriptions, or surveys.
rules.violation_condition: a blog post without a call to action at the end
rules.why: Clear structural requirement for blog posts supported by an example.
